doc.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: What Tin Pan Alley was
summary: He humorously describes the Brill Building songwriters and their songs about places they never visited; Rowe notes rock writers later worked there.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: For our younger viewers, can you tell us what tin pan alley means?

Oh, tin pan alley was basically, at first, there are books on it, first it was someplace else, but it wound up being the Brill Building on Broadway in midtown Manhattan, where guys— hi young viewers. Tin Pan Alley was where guys named Sid and Morty worked on out-of-tune pianos in little cubicles, smoked foul cigars, breathed on each other the foul cigars and tried to just get on top of the latest trend. When they had all these songs about, you know, if you don’t like ham that melts in your mouth, if you don’t like da, da, da, da, stay out of the south, and if you don’t— and they had that whole thing about that people called him Loving Sam, the sheik of Alabam, there’s a whole thing, everything, all the songs were about this— and as George S. Kaufmann once said about the twenties, he said, it was an era when all the Broadway sports got on the midnight choo choo for Alabama at Penn Station and got off in Newark. They’d never been south of Coney Island, these guys. Then when they wrote about Hawaii, on the beach at Waikiki and all this stuff, they had a couple of postcards, you know, that’s all. And during the war, you know, Rose O’Day and Johnny Doughboy [sings] found a rose in Ireland and all that stuff. These guys are still sitting up there pounding it out on their thing with the racing sheet in their back pocket.
That’s fascinating because later on the Brill Building became the home of some of the rock & roll writers too.
Yeah, Carole King, Neil Sedaka, they worked there. Probably the same room, it probably still smelled like cigar smoke.
Yeah. Only difference is now it’s pot.
Change the music a little bit.
